extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Agencies; agency officials responsible for implementing OMB policies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance to executive branch agencies on implementing OMB Circular A-76 to decide whether government activities should be performed in-house or contracted out, emphasizing cost comparisons, workforce impacts, and agency leadership in execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy preference for competitive private enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: This Administration strongly supports the general policy of reliance on competitive private enterprise to supply the products and services needed by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reliance on competitive private enterprise as a guiding policy when considering acquisition of commercial/industrial products and services; view contracting out as a tool to achieve economies and efficiencies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine the least cost method (contract or in-house)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining the least cost method of providing essential services (contract or in-house).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private performance is feasible and no overriding factors require in-house performance, a rigorous comparison of contract costs versus in-house costs will be made to determine whether work continues in-house or is converted to a contract operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Circular's Cost Comparison Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Circular's Cost Comparison Handbook to perform the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All cost comparisons should be made using the Cost Comparison Handbook specified by the Circular to ensure consistency and rigor in comparing contract and in-house costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum savings threshold for conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing in-house activities will not be converted to contract performance on the basis of economy unless it will result in a savings of at least 10 percent of the estimated Government personnel costs for the period of the comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require at least a 10% estimated personnel-cost savings over the comparative analysis period before converting an in-house activity to contract performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of first refusal for displaced federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal employees displaced as a result of the conversion to contract performance will be given the right of first refusal for employment openings in the contract operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide affected federal employees with priority consideration for jobs in the contractor operation when conversions occur, as an explicit protection in the implementation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of overriding factors requiring in-house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: When private performance of commercial or industrial activities is feasible and no overriding factors require in-house performance, a rigorous comparison will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and document any overriding factors (e.g., national security, statutory restrictions, essential mission needs) that justify retaining in-house performance despite cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline organizations for efficient performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamlining existing government organizations ensuring they are organized and staffed for the most efficient performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of implementation, agencies should reorganize and staff activities to achieve maximum internal efficiency before or alongside cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce long-range fiscal obligations when cost-effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing long-range fiscal obligations through reductions in the Federal workforce when cost comparisons show a contract operation is more cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cost-comparison outcomes to identify opportunities to lower long-term personnel obligations by converting appropriate activities to contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance productivity via measurable job standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancing productivity through the development of measurable job standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and apply measurable job standards as part of the evaluation and implementation process to improve productivity and enable fair comparisons between in-house and contract performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use contracting solely to circumvent personnel ceilings
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructions preclude the use of contracting with firms and institutions outside the Government solely to circumvent personnel ceilings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contracting decisions under A-76 are driven by legitimate cost-effectiveness and efficiency goals, not by attempts to evade statutory or administrative limits on civilian employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a structured and deliberate A-76 process
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies that contract out for goods and services under the structured and deliberate process prescribed by OMB Circular A-76 are doing so because it is cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the formal procedures and documentation requirements of Circular A-76 (structured/deliberate process) to validate that contracting decisions are appropriate and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency leadership and visible support for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular lacked requisite leadership and support from agency officials which is needed for effective implementation; agencies must become vigorously involved and provide overall leadership to fully implement the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior agency officials must actively lead, support, and provide the visibility necessary to implement A-76 effectively (targeted here to full implementation by the close of fiscal year 1982); OMB will issue a bulletin to assist and provide visibility.
